newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fuel firm CPN readies privatisation scheme.
newsitem.headline: Polish fuel firm CPN readies privatisation scheme.

text.p: Poland's largest fuels distributor, state-owned CPN SA, is preparing its own privatisation programme in case the government one is not implemented, its president said on Tuesday.

"At the end of this year CPN will be ready to submit an information memorandum to potential investors...we are now appraising our assets and settling legal problems," Jerzy Malyska told Reuters in an interview.

He said that under the company's scheme CPN could form a joint venture with a strategic investor or accept a passive investment, rather than be sold along with the country's seven refineries as envisaged by the government programme.
Malyska said CPN was preparing its scheme in case the government programme failed, because, for example, investors proved not to be interested in buying refineries and CPN jointly.
"A potential investor may say it is interested only in the (fuel distribution) market and then we will face a choice whether to privatise only the market or not privatise at all," he said.

Under the government programme, aimed at strengthening Poland's oil sector ahead of its opening to Western competition in the next few years, CPN and the refineries are to be grouped in a holding company, created in May and named Nafta Polska SA.
CPN is to be sold jointly with refineries, with initially a minority stake offered to foreign investors and then possibly extended.
Nafta Polska is to hold 75 percent stakes in the refineries and a 33 percent stake in CPN.

The refineries will hold the remaining 66 percent of CPN. Investors will be offered stakes directly in refineries and thus indirectly in CPN, which runs nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,700 petrol stations.
CPN plans to invest $500 million within five to seven years to build up to 400 petrol stations.
Malyska said the company's net profit forecast for 1996 is 94.8 million zlotys ($35.1 million).
In the first 11 month of last year CPN netted 109 million zlotys. No financial results are available for the whole of 1995 because the company changed its auditing procedures.
